name: Log Shattering / Combinatorial Eluder Dimension (logarithmic)
details: For every finite binary class with positive combinatorial eluder dimension, $\log_2|\operatorname{sh}(\mathcal H)|\geq\log_2\mathrm{Edim}(\mathcal H)$; more precisely it is at least $\log_2(\mathrm{Edim}(\mathcal H)+1)$.
proof: Let $(x_i,h_i)_{i=1}^m$ be an eluder witness relative to $h^*$.  The coordinates $x_i$ are distinct: if $x_i=x_j$ for $j<i$, the agreement condition for $h_i$ at $x_j$ contradicts its disagreement at $x_i$.  At each $x_i$, $h_i$ and $h^*$ realize both labels, so $\{x_i\}$ is shattered.  Thus the shattering family contains the empty set and these $m$ singleton sets, giving $|\operatorname{sh}(\mathcal H)|\geq m+1$.
witness_verification: For the trivial class $\mathcal T_n=\{\emptyset,[n]\}$, log shattering is $\log_2(n+1)$ while combinatorial eluder dimension is $1$; hence no reverse affine-linear bound holds.
